key_insight: SkillFuzz turns implicit-intent detection into a fuzzing problem over skill compositions, revealing that individually safe skills can interact to steer LLM agents toward unintended goals.
engineering_relevance: For open skill marketplaces, this provides an execution-free screening method to audit compositional risks before deployment and reduce security blind spots from isolated skill review.
method: Extract structured skill contracts from skill documents
Use contract-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search to prioritize suspicious skill compositions
Compare planning artifacts against a skill-free baseline as a differential oracle
evidence_signal: On representative workloads, SkillFuzz found over 1,000 implicit intents, confirmed more than 80% of the highest-risk flagged compositions during execution-time validation, and outperformed alternative search strategies while exploring only a fraction of the pairwise space.
watch_item: Effectiveness depends on the quality of extracted skill contracts and planning artifacts, so noisy or incomplete skill descriptions may reduce detection accuracy.
paper_title: SkillFuzz: Fuzzing Skill Composition for Implicit Intents Discovery in Open Skill Marketplaces
